name: ticket-tiers
title: Ticket tiers
description: Ticket types for an event with price, inclusions, how many are left and when the price rises, with sold out and not on sale yet designed as states.
docs: Pass the tiers (an id, a name, an optional description, the price in whole units, what is included, an optional remaining count, an optional saleStart and saleEnd as ISO times and an optional max per order), onSelect, and the currency, locale and timeZone prices and dates are written in. A tier that is sold out, ended or not on sale yet keeps its place with a disabled button and a clear label. An open tier shows how many are left, in the heavy style at or below lowStock, the date the price rises as a time element, a quantity stepper with the total, and a button that says how many tickets it buys. The stepper stops at the stock and at the limit per order; pressing plus at a limit keeps the button focusable and says why in words in a polite status line, which is also where the limit is stated before anyone hits it. Sale windows are judged on the reader's clock after mount, or on the now you pass. Until the clock is known, a tier that has a sale window shows as checking: no badge, a muted price and a disabled button that says Checking availability, so the server never renders a tier open that the browser would close. Pass now from the server and nothing is ever checking. A tier with no sale window is open straight away, and a sold-out one is sold out whatever the clock says. The badge has a row of its own above the name on every card, so names and descriptions line up however long a date is. The cards share their rows through a subgrid, so the prices, lists and buttons line up. The stepper is its own and not NumberInput, on purpose: its plus stays focusable at a limit and says why in words, where NumberInput disables its buttons and keeps them out of the tab order. labels translates the fixed words, Checking availability included.
